entry.name: Innkeeper in the Samaritan parable
entry.note: Unnamed host of the inn inside the story in Luke 10:35, entrusted with the injured traveler’s care and given two denarii. Distinct from the Samaritan, injured traveler and framing speakers.

result.appearanceFromText: The text fixes only that the host is an innkeeper who receives the injured traveler and is given two denarii; no physical appearance is described, so the look is supplied from the Roman-era Judean setting of the brief.

stages.label: Innkeeper
stages.when: Roman Judea, first century, the inn on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho

quotes.quote: he took out two denarii, gave them to the host, and said to him
He set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

stages.text: Innkeeper: a man of middle years, forties, sturdy and weathered from the roadside trade; medium build with broad, work-worn hands; olive skin, dark hair cropped short with a close-trimmed beard shot with grey; lined, steady face with an honest, practical bearing. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a dull brown wool cloak; earth-brown and ochre tones. Signature prop: a small leather purse at his belt holding coins.
